summary: A nostalgic reflection written in fall 2023 on how local education policies once united schools and their communities. It traces dated initiatives from 1993 to 2023, including parent volunteer programs, community projects, cultural festivals, PTA meetings, local mentors and a digital campaign. It concludes that education is a collective partnership among family, community and educators, and expresses a wish to revitalize those ties.
one_line: A look back at school-community programs from 1993 to 2023 that show education as a partnership of parents, communities and educators.
key_facts: On September 8, 1993, Principal Jane Thompson of Jefferson Elementary opened the school doors to the Parents in Education (PIE) program.
Parents Michael and Patricia Johnson volunteered in reading programs, aiding the inter-generational transfer of values and skills.
On October 15, 2001, State Education Commissioner Sarah Rodriguez implemented the "Community Classroom Connection" policy.
The Community Classroom Connection policy required each school to integrate at least two community-related projects every semester.
"Breakfast with Books" was hosted at Lincoln Middle School on November 12, 2004, bringing together local authors, parents and educators.
Hispanic Heritage Month began September 15, 2010, and the "Fiesta de la Educación" festival on September 20, 2010 included bilingual workshops for Spanish-speaking families.
"Wednesdays for the Future" was initiated on September 6, 2017, by the PTA at Riverside High School, chaired by Elaine Foster.
The "Local Legends to Classroom Mentors" program was inaugurated at Oakwood Community School on March 21, 2023, inviting trade experts, local historians and former astronauts.
The "Digital Bridge" campaign saw a considerable push starting in late September 2023 to equip parents and community members for the digital aspects of education.
Virtual book clubs and online school forums became the norm as technology replaced chalk and slate.
The note concludes that education is a collective endeavor, a partnership with the family, the community and every stakeholder.
